The '''Deck Master''' or '''DM''' was a [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who worked as Deck Master at the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] ''[[New Hope]]'' around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].

==History==
This human male had joined the Rebel Alliance by the beginning of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Civil War]]. By [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]] he had joined the forces of the ''[[New Hope]]'' being responsible for the hangar of the flagship.<ref name="sfte" />

According to his duties, he worked in a zone of the hangar that is marked with yellow-and-black stripes. He usually operated a tall [[exoskeleton]] with a voice amplifier and handled various operations, such as a crane. He was used in seeing mysterious civilians being assigned ships by his superiors, with disastrous results. Often worrying about his inventory and repair work, he often criticised them.<ref name="sfte" />

One day he served a [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]], a [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] and a [[Human/Legends|human]] who mostly requested for [[Maintenance droid/Legends|maintenance droids]] when finally [[Kyle Katarn]] approached him. Thinking that he also came for a droid, he warned him that they were unavailable, and as Katarn shouted something to him, he gripped him with his mechanical arms and lifted him up to his face's level. Katarn repeated that he came to select a ship, and while the Deck Master pointed out that not anyone can come and choose a ship as if it was a store, Katarn provided the requested [[Datacard/Legends|data card]], which he took with his actual hands and checked it with his mounted [[computer terminal]]. He gave him a [[Paper/Legends|printout]] with three hull numbers of the ships available to him. He returned Kyle to the ground, warning him that the Alliance would deduct the damages form his salary, and since he wasn't paid, from his skin.<ref name="sfte" />

Katarn eventually chose the ''[[Moldy Crow/Legends|Moldy Crow]]'' and while preparing for a [[mission to Danuta]], he "borrowed" dozens of tools, parts, and components from storerooms and surrounding ships; this was tolerated by the Deck Master, at [[Jan Ors]]'s request, who was monitoring him.<ref name="sfte" />

==Character and traits==
The Deck Master was a man that often forgot or was too busy to shave, even for days and could be seen with some [[Hair/Legends|beard]]. Perhaps because of the working conditions and nature of his duties he had red eyes, visible under his bushy eyebrows.<ref name="sfte" />

Usually he would be seen in the cage of his exoskeleton suit, doing various operations, like giving orders to crane operators. The suit was ten meters tall and his position was known by the title "Deck Master" [[Writing/Legends|written]] on the chest plate. It had a voice amplifier (curiously not a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]]) so that his orders were heard over the hangar's noise. His roll cage also had a mounted computer terminal, with which he could keep a toll of ship assignments.<ref name="sfte" />

He didn't appreciate much of his superior officers, or as he called them the "metal heads on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]]" as their thoughtless decisions apparently brought trouble to his work and inventory; especially he didn't think that allowing non-[[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], such as [[Agent/Legends|agents]] and other civilians, should be assigned ships, as in the best of cases they returned them heavily damaged.<ref name="sfte" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You've got to be joking. This isn't even a ship! Hey, I thought you said this thing would get off the ground!''"<br />"''It will. But after that, I'm not making any promises.|Kyle Katarn to the deck master at his first sighting of the ''Crow''|audio=MoldyCrowFirstLook-DFSftE.flac|<ref name="sfte audio">[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire (audio drama)|''Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
The Deck Master appears in the ''[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire]]'' and its [[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire (audio drama)|audio drama]]. Whereas in the novel he appears busy and operating an exoskeleton, in the audio drama he is only operating a noisy [[welding torch]] which he turns off before talking to Katarn. Whereas in the novel he says that the hangar is not a shop, in the audio drama he says it is not "a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt's]] trophy room". Instead of a datacard, Katarn provides a paper from [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], and then, instead of directing him to three ships to choose from, he directly points him to the ship at slot number three, ensuring him that she could take off the ground. Upon seeing the ''Crow'', Katarn expresses his skepticism that it could fly; the Deck Master admitted that it didn't look much.
